steps.say: The classical complement pathway is triggered by immune complexes binding C1q. Profound congenital deficiency of early components, C1q, C1r, C1s and C4, carries an extraordinary risk of developing severe systemic lupus erythematosus, exceeding ninety percent in homozygous C1q deficiency, because apoptotic debris is not cleared. Missing early parts means uncleared debris and lupus.
steps.tx: The **classical complement pathway** is triggered by immune complexes binding **C1q**. Profound congenital deficiency of early components (C1q, C1r, C1s, C4) carries an extraordinary risk of severe systemic lupus erythematosus, exceeding **90%** in homozygous C1q deficiency, because **apoptotic debris** is not cleared. Missing early parts means uncleared debris and lupus.

vis.alt: Classical, lectin and alternative complement pathways converging on C3 and the membrane attack complex that lyses Neisseria; the MHC panels are not taught.
vis.caption: Only the complement panel is taught; the MHC panels are the drawing. Deficiency risks are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: The alternative complement pathway is initiated by spontaneous tick-over hydrolysis of C3 into C3 water, and stabilized on microbial surfaces by factor B and properdin. Unchecked alternative pathway activity caused by autoantibodies against C3 convertase, called C3 nephritic factor, leads to membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and dense deposit disease. Tick-over that never stops scars the glomerulus.
steps.tx: The **alternative complement pathway** is initiated by spontaneous tick-over hydrolysis of **C3** into C3(H2O) and stabilized on microbial surfaces by **factor B** and properdin. Unchecked alternative pathway activity caused by autoantibodies against C3 convertase (**C3 nephritic factor**) leads to **membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis** and dense deposit disease. Tick-over that never stops scars the glomerulus.

vis.alt: Glomerular capillary with ribbon-like dense deposits in the basement membrane in C3 glomerulopathy.
vis.caption: Ribbon dense deposits of C3 glomerulopathy. The nephritic factor mechanism is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: The membrane attack complex is assembled from terminal complement components, C5b through C9. Inherited deficiencies of C5, C6, C7, C8, or C9 confer a markedly heightened susceptibility to recurrent disseminated infections with encapsulated Neisseria species, meningococcus and gonococcus. Susceptible bacteria are lysed by the end of the cascade.
steps.tx: Terminal complement components (**C5b through C9**) assemble into the **membrane attack complex**. Inherited deficiencies of C5, C6, C7, C8, or C9 confer a markedly heightened susceptibility to recurrent disseminated infections with encapsulated **Neisseria** species (N. meningitidis and N. gonorrhoeae). Susceptible bacteria are lysed by the end of the cascade.

steps.say: Depressed serum C3 and C4 levels reflect active immune complex-mediated consumption. Profound hypocomplementemia is characteristic of active proliferative lupus nephritis, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, and subacute bacterial endocarditis. Falling levels with active urine sediment mean the kidney is under immune attack.
steps.tx: Depressed serum **C3 and C4** levels reflect active immune complex-mediated **consumption**. Profound **hypocomplementemia** characteristically accompanies active proliferative **lupus nephritis**, cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, and subacute bacterial endocarditis. Falling levels with active urine sediment mean the kidney is under immune attack.

vis.alt: Glomerulus with wire loop lesions, endocapillary and mesangial proliferation, and immune complexes in lupus nephritis.
vis.caption: Wire loops and proliferation in lupus nephritis. Consumption patterns are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: C-reactive protein is a pentameric pattern recognition acute-phase protein synthesized by hepatocytes under direct stimulation by interleukin six, with a short plasma half-life of nineteen hours. It is an exquisite, rapid-responding indicator of systemic inflammation, bacterial infection, and treatment response. A fast rise and fast fall make it the activity tracker.
steps.tx: **C-reactive protein** (CRP) is a pentameric pattern recognition acute-phase protein synthesized by hepatocytes under direct stimulation by **IL-6**, with a short plasma half-life of **19 hours**, making it an exquisite, rapid-responding indicator of systemic inflammation, bacterial infection, and treatment response. A fast rise and fast fall make it the activity tracker.

rows: Made in liver under IL-6, half-life 19 hours, rises and falls fast

steps.say: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate measures the settling velocity of erythrocytes and depends primarily on asymmetric plasma proteins, especially fibrinogen. A marked dissociation of high ESR with normal or low CRP is a classic diagnostic clue pointing toward active lupus flare, multiple myeloma, or severe hypergammaglobulinemia. When the two disagree, the pattern is believed, not one number.
steps.tx: **Erythrocyte sedimentation rate** (ESR) measures the settling velocity of erythrocytes and depends primarily on asymmetric plasma proteins, especially **fibrinogen**. A marked dissociation of **high ESR with normal or low CRP** is a classic diagnostic clue pointing toward active **lupus flare**, multiple myeloma, or severe hypergammaglobulinemia. When the two disagree, the pattern is believed, not one number.

points: High with normal CRP means lupus, myeloma, gammopathy
right.title: ESR

steps.say: Extreme hyperferritinemia exceeding ten thousand nanograms per millilitre is an urgent diagnostic marker of macrophage activation syndrome, that is secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, adult-onset Still disease, catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, and severe septic shock with multiorgan failure. Ferritin at that height is never incidental and always triggers a hunt.
steps.tx: Extreme **hyperferritinemia** exceeding **10,000 ng/mL** is an urgent diagnostic marker of **macrophage activation syndrome** (secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis), adult-onset Still disease, catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, and severe septic shock with multiorgan failure. Ferritin at that height is never incidental and always triggers a hunt.

vis.alt: Cytokine storm with haemophagocytic macrophages engulfing erythrocytes in macrophage activation syndrome.
vis.caption: Cytokine storm and haemophagocytosis. The ferritin threshold is in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Cryoglobulins are immunoglobulins that precipitate reversibly at temperatures below thirty seven degrees Celsius. Brouet classification stratifies them into Type one, isolated monoclonal immunoglobulin, associated with multiple myeloma and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia; Type two, mixed monoclonal IgM with rheumatoid factor activity plus polyclonal IgG, linked to hepatitis C; and Type three, polyclonal IgM and IgG. Type by clonality, then look for the cause.
steps.tx: **Cryoglobulins** are immunoglobulins that precipitate reversibly at temperatures below **37 degrees Celsius**. Brouet classification stratifies them into **Type I** (isolated monoclonal Ig, associated with multiple myeloma and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia), **Type II** (mixed monoclonal IgM with rheumatoid factor activity plus polyclonal IgG, linked to hepatitis C), and **Type III** (polyclonal IgM and IgG). Type by clonality, then look for the cause.

vis.alt: Vessel with cryoglobulin precipitates, neutrophil infiltration and fibrinoid necrosis beside palpable purpura on the legs.
vis.caption: Precipitates, vessel injury and purpura in cryoglobulinaemic vasculitis. Types and associations are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).
